summary:
Innovation Orbit – AI-Powered Fire Hotspot Monitoring Platform

Innovation Orbit is an Earth observation project designed to harmonize active fire hotspot data from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite sensors. These satellites provide valuable information about wildfires and agricultural burning, but differences in spatial resolution, observation times, and data formats make direct comparison difficult.

Our project aims to bring these observations into a unified platform to provide a consistent view of fire activity across different locations and time periods. It processes hotspot information such as latitude, longitude, acquisition date, time, confidence level, and Fire Radiative Power (FRP).

Using data analysis, AI/ML techniques, and interactive data visualization, the platform aims to identify historical fire patterns, unusual hotspot activity, and potential fire-risk periods.

Innovation Orbit aims to support researchers, environmental authorities, and emergency response teams with better satellite-based information for fire monitoring and disaster management.
details: 1. Problem Statement Fire outbreaks and wildfires can cause severe damage to forests, wildlife, human lives, and the environment. MODIS and VIIRS satellites provide active fire hotspot observations, but differences in their spatial resolution, observation times, and data formats make direct comparison difficult. 2. Proposed Solution Our project, Innovation Orbit, proposes an AI-driven Earth observation platform that combines MODIS and VIIRS active fire hotspot observations into a unified system. It aims to provide a clear view of fire activity across different locations and time periods. 3. NASA Satellite Data The project uses NASA satellite-based active fire observations from: - MODIS – Terra and Aqua satellites. - VIIRS – Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21. 4. Data Processing The proposed system processes satellite hotspot records, including latitude, longitude, acquisition date, time, confidence and fire radiative power (FRP). It aims to organize observations into a consistent dataset for analysis. 5. AI and Machine Learning AI/ML techniques can help analyze historical fire activity, identify unusual hotspot patterns and support fire-risk analysis. The final implementation will depend on the available training data and validation. 6. Data Visualization The planned interactive dashboard will display hotspot locations on a map, historical fire activity, location-based filtering and time-based fire activity patterns. 7. Expected Impact The proposed platform aims to support researchers, environmental authorities, emergency responders and disaster management teams through better access to satellite-based fire information. 8. Future Scope Future development may include improved fire activity forecasting, automated alerts, additional satellite datasets and integration with other environmental hazard monitoring systems.
